lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: sample spaces, unions, intersections, and complements

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: Group X: 12 successes, 8 failures. Find P(success | X).

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: Two events have P(A) = 3/10, P(B) = 4/10, and P(A and B) = 13/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.

items.prompt: In a group of 21, 10 do activity A, 11 do activity B, and 6 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 2/6 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 22 successes and 20 failures; group Y with 6 successes and 12 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 9/10, P(B) = 7/10, and P(A and B) = 68/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: In a group of 36, 22 do activity A, 18 do activity B, and 10 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 1/4 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
